Martin — attaching the walkthrough deliverables we discussed. Quick executive summary up front: Redwood separates control and data planes, enforces per-tenant network demarcation, and maintains a strict least-privilege model for runtime sidecars and control-plane APIs. Below are the highlights and the adversary-model summary we will present on Thursday.

--- Executive highlights (TL;DR) ---
- Tenancy model: Each private deployment gets an isolated VPC/namespace; Dedicated pools are logically partitioned and enforce per-job credentials. Hosted customers share runtime clusters but are isolated via per-request authentication, KV-cache scoping and tenant-aware request routing.
- Control plane: A customer-facing control plane (multi-tenant) is logically separate from the data path; telemetry and management APIs authenticate with short-lived mTLS client certs and are encrypted in transit.
- Egress controls: Default-deny egress with allowlists per-deployment; optional egress-proxy sidecar for additional inspection in Private deployments.
- KV cache and memory: KV caches are keyed by tenant and wiped on tenancy teardown; we run per-tenant cache namespaces and memory limits to reduce cross-tenant data remnants.
- Logging & evidence: Per-tenant structured logs, request tracing with immutable timestamps (W3C trace-context), and audit bundles we can export for compliance review.

--- Adversary model summary ---
We target three primary threat vectors relevant to EdgeBank's risk profile:
1) Cross-tenant data exposure (misrouting, shared memory leakage) — mitigations: strict kernel-level guardrails in runtime, tenant-scoped KV namespaces, and periodic memory-zeroing of terminated sessions.
2) Control-plane compromise enabling tenant impersonation — mitigations: mTLS with short lifetimes, KMS-backed key rotation, RBAC minimization, and separate service accounts for topology changes vs. runtime request routing.
3) Egress/sidecar compromise enabling data exfiltration — mitigations: allowlist egress, deep-packet inspection optional via sidecar, and circuit-breakers that fail closed to a safe-mode model variant (lower-capacity, no external connectors).

Operational notes: for on-prem Private installs we ship a hardened sidecar image and provide a deployment checklist that includes host hardening, kernel module allowlist, and network ACL recommendations. For Hosted we recommend using our Dedicated plan if you require stronger per-tenant hardware boundaries.

Attachments included: redwood-deployment-annotated-diagram.pdf (diagram, annotated attack paths), redwood-egress-controls-evidence.pdf (policy screenshots & sample allowlist), redwood-deployment-summary.pdf (one-page summary).

On Thu we'll walk through the annotated diagram and capture any diagram edits you want.

Best,
Irene

Irene — thanks for the fast packet. A few clarifying questions before the walkthrough:

1) For Private on-prem installs: can the egress-proxy be constrained to a single outbound IP per deployment (we need static egress for allowlisting)?
2) How do you demonstrate that KV cache keys cannot be used to cross-retrieve tenant artifacts (we'd like a short test plan or screenshots showing cache namespace separation)?
3) Control-plane access: do you have SOC2 evidence for short-lived cert rotation and the KMS integration?
4) Could you produce a version of the diagram that highlights the ingress path for requests originating from our internal network (we need to show our compliance team exactly where TLS terminates and which hops see plaintext)?

If you can provide the three artifacts below before Thu that'd accelerate procurement: a PDF with an ingress-focused diagram, a short test plan or screenshot showing KV namespaces, and a link to the SOC2 evidence bundle or a contact for compliance review.

Regards,
Martin

- SOC2 evidence: we have an evidence export bundle (SOC2-2024-bundle.zip) stored on the security drive. I'll link the share during the call.
- Diagram: produce an ingress-focused copy annotating TLS termination point and which internal components see plaintext. Use the existing annotated PDF as the base; add a callout box for EdgeBank's on-prem network flow.

Attachments to prepare before Thu: redwood-ingress-path-edgebank.pdf (new), kv-namespace-screenshot.png (sanitized), SOC2-evidence-link (drive).

I'll take the diagram edit and the kv screenshot; Jordan, can you confirm egress static-IP behavior by EOD?

—Stephanie

Stephanie / Irene — quick update: for Redwood Private we can support single static egress IP per deployment when customers route through an included NAT gateway. For fully air-gapped on-prem installs customers can place the NAT on their side; for managed Private in our hosted colo we can allocate a static IP via our egress-proxy NAT pool (requires a short provisioning lead, typically 48–72 hours).

I'll also pull a sanitized kv-namespace screenshot from staging and drop it into the Drive folder (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink).
